criteria._comment: Everything about the report except the readings - the location, the client, the instrument, and above all WHICH reference profile was chosen per parameter - was typed into MonitoringReportSheet and discarded when it closed. So the issued session now rides the sensorData envelope (which already persists to draft, report and cloud) and lib/jasper/monitoring-report-summary.ts re-derives the exact document through buildMonitoringReportModel - the same pure function the DOCX renderer calls. Reading the model beats extracting our own DOCX on every axis: lossless, exact, and cheap. Scope is EXPLAIN, not review: the tool ships usage_rules because neither that nor the locked status vocabulary can be enforced by a data shape. The load-bearing property is that a comparison the report WITHHELD (calibration not covering the period, status Not Established) can never reach Jasper as within/above/outside - the statistics still print, so that is the easiest misreading in the document.

criteria.label: Every published threshold is reconciled against an independent record, and every reference line traces to a criterion
criteria._comment: The systemic answer to two fabricated citations. Numbers live in constants/criteria.js (machine) and constants/standards-corpus.js (curated prose with primary-source citations), authored independently. Nothing compared them, so the engine scored temperature against an invented 67-82 F band for four months while the corpus three directories away carried the correct 68-76 / 73-79 and had done all along. standards-reconciliation.test.ts requires a declared figure to match the registry EXACTLY and requires every criterion to be either documented or named in a visible gap ledger with a reason - there is no third state. reference-line-provenance.test.ts requires every rendered reference line to resolve to a criterion, in the criterion's value, under the criterion's citation. Both are run by BUILD-02; these checks assert they exist and are wired, because a guard nobody runs is the failure mode that produced this criterion.

checks._comment: The corpus half of the ledger. Without declared figures the reconciliation has nothing to compare and passes vacuously.
Band criteria. Temperature and humidity had no registry entry because the registry could only express value > threshold, and they are the only two parameters whose citations were wrong.

criteria.label: An over-reaching sentence retired in the phrase library is retired in the engine that actually ships it
criteria._comment: src/engine/report/phrases/ decides what may be said about a condition, but it is read by renderClientReport and PrintReport only. The AtmosFlow DOCX - the sole client deliverable since 2026-08 - renders raw text from scoring.js and scoring-legacy.js via reportModel.collectFindings and genRecs. So three retirements were written down, believed, and went on shipping anyway: the automatic Legionella / ASHRAE 188 escalation (fired by one intake dropdown, citing a standard scoped to aerosol-generating water systems, and closing by ASSERTING occupant respiratory symptoms nothing had recorded), the automatic EPA-registered-biocide instruction, and the ATSDR occupant-risk-communication action. Each surfaced only because somebody read a screenshot. editorial-engine-parity.test.ts makes the general property machine-checkable - no engine finding may contain a bannedAlternative of the condition type it classifies to - and pins the three named retirements at the engine, at collectFindings and in genRecs. It also asserts what must REMAIN, because an absence-only guard is satisfied by an engine that recommends nothing at all.

checks._comment: Anchored to a single-quoted STRING LITERAL, not the bare words. The runner does not strip comments, and both files carry removal records that name Legionella and quote the retired sentence in full - the unanchored form matched 4 of those comment lines, which is the exact false-positive class NO-COMPOSITE-SCORE was already re-anchored to avoid. Verified both ways: 0 hits on the current files, 4 hits on a fixture carrying the original literals. Finding-level and recommendation-level detection lives in the two tests above, which BUILD-02 runs.
The general half. Without it this criterion degrades into three string checks that say nothing about the fourth remnant.

criteria.label: TVOC is measured, charted and reported, and compared against nothing
criteria._comment: The Molhave 1991 advisory tiers (500 / 3,000 ug/m3) were the only basis on which this platform judged a total-VOC reading, and they were not a limit - they are a chamber-study dose-response framework, and no regulatory or consensus health-based limit exists for a non-specific sum that identifies no compound. Applying them produced a severity, a citation, a client-facing finding, a live field advisory, a sampling trigger and a causal-chain term. All of it was removed in 2026-08, together with the WELL v2 target that offered a third yardstick. Captioning a tier 'advisory' is what let it spread: a figure printed beside a measured value reads as a limit however it is labelled, and every surface that carried one also carried a disclaimer. no-molhave.test.ts pins the class rather than the instances - behavioural assertions through the real entry points at every tier boundary, plus a source sweep for a TVOC threshold in a rendered position with comments stripped, because twenty-odd files now carry removal records that name the figures and a guard that could not tell a record from a string would fire on its own documentation. It also pins what must REMAIN: the reading is still captured and unit-converted, the report says 'not evaluated' rather than 'acceptable', and the renovation-source TO-17 sampling entry still fires (it keys on a recorded source, not a concentration).

checks._comment: Anchored to the SHAPES a reintroduction would take - the STD.c.tvoc constant block, and a criterion or profile declared as `id: 'molhave...'` / `id: 'tvoc_molhave...'` - rather than the bare word. The runner does not strip comments and every one of these files now carries a removal record naming the tiers, their figures and their old ids; the unanchored form matched one of those records on the first run, which is the same false-positive class NO-COMPOSITE-SCORE and EDITORIAL-ENGINE-PARITY were both re-anchored to avoid. Verified both ways: 0 hits on the current tree, and a hit on each file when the constant block, the criterion or the profile is put back.

The general half. Without the source sweep - and without its two exemptions, one for removal records and one for the strings that FORBID the comparison - this criterion degrades into a handful of greps that say nothing about the next surface somebody adds.

criteria.label: The 100-point composite, its category weights and every risk band are absent from every layer they reached
criteria._comment: Modelled on MOLD-UI-NO-HEALTH-VERDICT: an exclusion pair plus the positive assertion of what replaced it. The patterns match CODE SHAPES (an export declaration, a constant assignment, an object key) because every file involved carries a comment recording what was removed from it, and that record must not be what fails the gate. Band-ladder detection needs comment stripping and so lives in tests/engine/no-scoring.test.ts, which this criterion runs. Test-suite run removed 2026-09: BUILD-02 runs `npm test` once for the whole config (it used to run eight times, ~10 minutes). The suite files this criterion relies on are asserted by the file_exists checks.

checks.pattern: >[^<]*(Transparent Scoring Summary|Max Points|priority-weighted mean|AtmosFlow applies a deterministic scoring methodology)|'Appendix B [^']*Transparent Scoring
checks._comment: The methodology PROSE, not just the arithmetic. PrintReport.jsx published 'Appendix B — Transparent Scoring Summary' — the composite formula, the 25/25/20/15/15 point caps and a 1.5x weight for data halls — in a client deliverable for four months after v3.0 removed the score, and every check here stayed green. Two reasons, both now closed: the checks matched code shapes while this was rendered text, and the one guard that did sweep the file (no-scoring.test.ts) hunted for comparison operators that an HTML template writes as < entities. That test now decodes entities and matches prose; this criterion is the independent second pair of eyes, because a single guard that can be blinded is not a guard. The pattern is anchored to a RENDERED shape — the phrase must follow a '>' inside a tag, or sit in the toc.push string literal — because the acceptance runner greps raw text with no comment stripping, and every file involved carries a removal record naming the section. Verified both ways before it was wired in: it matches all five of the lines that actually shipped, and none of the removal-record comments that describe them.
The report index and the cloud row stop WRITING a score. Their columns and their existing data are deliberately kept.
